results.title: Strengthening Causal Inference with Sensitivity Analyses: Using the Bayesian Parametric G-Formula - Phastar
results.content: # Strengthening Causal Inference with Sensitivity Analyses: Using the Bayesian Parametric G-Formula. Understanding causal relationships in real-world data is challenging, particularly in observational studies, where confounding can introduce bias. Two popular approaches to achieve this are inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and the parametric g-formula. This webinar will focus on using the Bayesian parametric g-formula as a sensitivity analysis for measured confounding. This allows for a better understanding of the range of the plausible effects. This approach offers a practical solution for researchers to ensure the validity of findings. * How Bayesian methods improve sensitivity analyses. Watch this webinar recording and explore how the Bayesian Parametric G-Formula can be used as a sensitivity analysis tool to strengthen causal inference and improve the validity of findings. Join us for the next webinar in our causal inference series, focusing on how regulatory bodies are incorporating caus... Causal Inference in Real World Evidence: What is it? Title: Variable Weighting via Multidimensional IRT Models in Composite Indicators Construction | Social Indicators Research | Springer Nature Link
# Variable Weighting via Multidimensional IRT Models in Composite Indicators Construction. In this paper, we introduce a new endogenous weighting methodology developed in an extended Item Response Theory (IRT) framework. As weighting is much more thorough when carried out by accounting for the dimensionality of a dataset rather than by ignoring it, we suggest to assign weights on the basis of the discrimination parameters estimated through a multidimensional two-parameter logistic IRT model. The second estimates the discrimination parameters under the multidimensional two-parameter logistic model selected at the first step. The potentialities of this novel weighting technique are illustrated through an application to educational data, which refer to a national standardised test developed and collected by the Italian National Institute for the Evaluation of the Education System. ## Access this article. ### The Role of Extended IRT Models for Composite Indicators Construction. ### A Nonparametric Multidimensional Latent Class IRT Model in a Bayesian Framework. results.title: The South Africa Social Cohesion Index: Measuring the well-being of a society - 2024 UPDATE
results.content: Table 3.1 Social cohesion and its dimensions in South Africa across time. Table 3.2 The overall index of social cohesion in South African provinces across time. Correlational analyses on the provinces’ overall level of social cohesion and their structural characteristics offer insights on how to strengthen social cohesion: by enabling inclusive (people-centered) economic progress, reducing unemployment, lowering income inequality, providing adequate jobs for the highly qualified, promoting a family-oriented life-style, and bringing the living conditions in rural and urban areas to an equally adequate level. The preferred LCA solution identifies four classes of South Africans: Class 1 (Critics), which is characterized by high Identification but critically low Acceptance of diversity, a critically low perception of Respect for social rules, and low to moderate scores on the other dimensions; Class 2 (Integrated Sceptics), which is characterized by well-knit Social networks, high levels of Trust in people, Acceptance of diversity, Solidarity, and Civic participation, but low scores on the remaining dimensions; Class 3 (Middle South Africa), which is characterized by a high level of Identification with the country but moderate scores on all other dimensions; and Class 4 (Cohesive Communities), which is an ideal-typical model of strong cohesion in South Africa manifesting itself in exceptionally high Identification and high scores on all other dimensions. In this section, we report findings on the level and trend of social cohesion in South Africa and its nine constituent provinces from 2021 to 2024. ***Table 1.5*** *Social cohesion and its dimensions in South Africa across time*. ***Table 1.6****The overall index of social cohesion in South African provinces across time*. Perception of fairness and Respect for social rules – the major weaknesses of social cohesion in South Africa – as well as Trust in institutions also register predominantly declines across the provinces. The previous sections of the report examined the levels and trends of social cohesion in South Africa and its provinces. Class 4, encompassing only 10.5 % of the respondents, exhibits a high level of social cohesion with an average score on the overall index of 73.3 points. This Appendix contains results on the level and change over time in the nine single dimensions of social cohesion across the provinces of South Africa.
